<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD's global scope only defines variables (`pkgname`, `pkgver`, `sha256sums`, etc.) and a `package()` function. No top-level command substitutions, `pkgver()` function, or other code that would execute during `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare`. The single source is a tarball from the official npm registry (`https://registry.npmjs.org/@devcontainers/cli/-/cli-0.89.0.tgz`) with a provided SHA-256 checksum (not SKIP). The `noextract` directive means the archive is downloaded but not extracted. All potentially dangerous operations (npm install, chown, sed) are inside `package()` and will not run during this stage. Therefore, fetching sources and sourcing the PKGBUILD is safe.
</details>
<evidence></evidence>
<summary>Safe: no global code, source is expected.</summary>
</security_assessment>
